authors.bio: William A. Hill is a senior engineer with experience in semiconductor device physics and CCD design dating back to 1970. He developed the CCD and its support electronics for this project. He is employed by Lockheed Martin's San Jose operations. Hill has an M.S. in physics from California State University at Los Angeles.
authors.name: W. A. Hill

authors.bio: Stephen A. Stough has developed specialized microwave and high-speed digital systems since 1973. He is the chief technology officer for the western region of Lockheed Martin Management & Data Systems in San Jose, CA. He is a member of the IEEE and the SMPTE. Stough has a B.A. degree in physics from the University of California at Berkeley.
authors.name: S. A. Stough

authors.bio: Troy A. Pellizzer has worked with RF analog and high-speed digital circuits and systems at Ford Aerospace, Space Systems Loral, Ashtech, and Lockheed Martin since 1982. Currently, he designs and develops circuits for very high rate data transmitters. He received a BSEE degree from Cogswell Polytechnical College in 1994.
authors.name: T. Pellizzer

authors.bio: Gregory A. Garcia has 16 years of experience working as a software engineer for Hughes Aircraft Company, Rockwell International, Lockheed Martin, Raytheon Corp., and Goodrich Aerospace. He is currently a software consultant. His areas of expertise include software systems design and integration, problem solving, digital image processing, and computer graphics. Garcia has a B.S. degree in computer science from California State Polytechnic University in Pomona, CA.
authors.name: G. Garcia

authors.bio: Steve N. Persall is a senior illustrator/photographer with 22 years of experience in graphics, multimedia production, image processing, and workflow management. He worked the system storage and network architectures, color management, and post-production for the Lockheed Martin 4K-24P camera. He has been employed by Lockheed Martin Management & Data Systems in San Jose since 1990.
authors.name: S. Persall

authors.bio: Gary S. Nunes has expertise in digital electronic and logic design and is a member of the Blue Herring EO camera system intgration team. He has a B.S. degree in electrical engineering from the University of California at Davis and a B.A. in management engineering from Claremont McKenna College. Nunes has been employed by Lockheed Martin M&DS in San Jose since 1999.
authors.name: G. Nunes

authors.bio: Kazunori Kushida is currently working on optical QPSK modems and the 12M pixel 24p digital cinema camera at Lockheed Martin Management & Data Systems in San Jose. He has a B.S. degree in electrical engineering from Georgia Tech.
authors.name: K. Kushida
